sn35.241:0.3: The Simile of the Great Log (1)
sn35.241:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Kosambī on the bank of the river Ganges.
sn35.241:1.2: The Blessed One saw a great log being carried along by the current of the river Ganges,
sn35.241:1.3: and he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn35.241:1.4: “Do you see, bhikkhus, that great log being carried along by the current of the river Ganges?”
sn35.241:1.6: “If, bhikkhus, that log does not veer towards the near shore, does not veer towards the far shore, does not sink in mid-stream, does not get cast up on high ground, does not get caught by human beings, does not get caught by nonhuman beings, does not get caught in a whirlpool, and does not become inwardly rotten,
sn35.241:1.7: it will slant, slope, and incline towards the ocean.
sn35.241:1.9: Because the current of the river Ganges slants, slopes, and inclines towards the ocean.
sn35.241:2.1: “So too, bhikkhus, if you do not veer towards the near shore, do not veer towards the far shore, do not sink in mid-stream, do not get cast up on high ground, do not get caught by human beings, do not get caught by nonhuman beings, do not get caught in a whirlpool,
sn35.241:2.2: and do not become inwardly rotten,
sn35.241:2.3: you will slant, slope, and incline towards Nibbāna.
sn35.241:2.5: Because right view slants, slopes, and inclines towards Nibbāna.”
sn35.241:2.6: When this was said, a certain bhikkhu asked the Blessed One:
sn35.241:2.7: “What, venerable sir, is the near shore? What is the far shore? What is sinking in mid-stream? What is getting cast up on high ground? What is getting caught by human beings, what is getting caught by nonhuman beings, what is getting caught in a whirlpool? What is inward rottenness?”
sn35.241:3.1: “‘The near shore,’ bhikkhu: this is a designation for the six internal sense bases.
sn35.241:3.2: ‘The far shore’: this is a designation for the six external sense bases.
sn35.241:3.3: ‘Sinking in mid-stream’: this is a designation for delight and lust.
sn35.241:3.4: ‘Getting cast up on high ground’: this is a designation for the conceit ‘I am.’
sn35.241:4.1: “And what, bhikkhu, is getting caught by human beings?
sn35.241:4.2: Here, someone lives in association with laypeople; he rejoices with them and sorrows with them, he is happy when they are happy and sad when they are sad, and he involves himself in their affairs and duties.
sn35.241:4.3: This is called getting caught by human beings.
sn35.241:5.1: “And what, bhikkhu, is getting caught by nonhuman beings?
sn35.241:5.2: Here, someone lives the holy life with the aspiration to be reborn into a certain order of devas, thinking: ‘By this virtue or vow or austerity or holy life I will become a deva or one among the devas.’
sn35.241:5.3: This is called getting caught by nonhuman beings.
sn35.241:5.4: “‘Getting caught in a whirlpool’: this, bhikkhu, is a designation for the five cords of sensual pleasure.
sn35.241:6.2: Here someone is immoral, one of evil character, of impure and suspect behaviour, secretive in his acts, no ascetic though claiming to be one, not a celibate though claiming to be one, inwardly rotten, corrupt, depraved.
sn35.241:7.1: Now on that occasion the cowherd Nanda was standing near the Blessed One.
sn35.241:7.2: He then said to the Blessed One:
sn35.241:7.3: “Venerable sir, I will not veer towards the near shore, I will not veer towards the far shore, I will not sink in mid-stream, I will not get cast up on high ground, I will not get caught by human beings, I will not get caught by nonhuman beings, I will not get caught in a whirlpool, I will not become inwardly rotten.
sn35.241:7.4: May I receive the going forth under the Blessed One, may I receive the higher ordination?”
sn35.241:7.5: “In that case, Nanda, return the cows to their owners.”
sn35.241:7.6: “The cows will go back of their own accord, venerable sir, out of attachment to the calves.”
sn35.241:7.7: “Return the cows to their owners, Nanda.”
sn35.241:7.8: Then the cowherd Nanda returned the cows to their owners, came back to the Blessed One, and said: “The cows have been returned to their owners,
sn35.241:7.10: May I receive the going forth under the Blessed One, may I receive the higher ordination?”
sn35.241:7.11: Then the cowherd Nanda received the going forth under the Blessed One, and he received the higher ordination.
sn35.241:7.12: And soon, not long after his higher ordination, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute …
sn35.241:7.13: the Venerable Nanda became one of the arahants.”
